# Glyph reference

Each glyph has a name, which links to its definitions and examples. A function glyph also has a name for its monad, which takes one argument, and for its dyad, which takes two. Operators take functions or arrays and derive functions. Notes flag unusual differences from Dyalog APL. Follow each glyph's link for details and examples. Each function's page gives its ranks. An argument of higher rank applies the function to each cell of that rank, as [Rank](glyphs/jot-diaeresis.qmd) does.

## Typing glyphs

The [keyboard map](keyboard.qmd) shows the Option and Option-Shift bindings, with dead keys outlined in orange.

Hold Alt, which is Option on a Mac, and press the key in the Key column. Keys refer to a US layout. `≤` is Alt-< and `≥` is Alt->, each with Shift held. Where the column shows a second key, press it with or without Alt held. For example, `Alt-o c` means Alt-o, then `c`. You can type a shifted second key without Shift. For example, `Alt-q ;` types `⍠`, the same as `Alt-q :`. An Alt key that takes a second key types its own glyph when Space or an unlisted key follows. For example, Alt-o then Space gives `○`. Backspace or Escape cancels the sequence.

Superscripts start with Alt-6. The second key is a digit, `-` then a digit, `t` for `ᵀ`, `u` for `ᵘ`, or `b` for `ᵇ`. Subscripts start with Alt-5. The second key is a digit, `-` then a digit, or `x`, `j`, `e` or `r` for the number suffixes `ₓ`, `ⱼ`, `ₑ` and `ᵣ`. A glyph with no key, such as `+`, is on an ordinary ASCII key. The arrows are on hjkl. Alt-[ types nothing, because terminals send it as the start of a control sequence. The identifier characters `∆` and `⍙` are Alt-7, and Alt-Minus then `7`.

The names in these tables are the ones you type. In the REPL, a backtick and any of them, then Tab, enters the glyph, as [named entry](repl.qmd#named-entry) describes. Python exports the function names, with `_` in place of `-` and a trailing `_` on Python keywords, as in `index_of` and `and_`. It spells operators as properties with their names, as in `f.reduce`.

## Monadic operators

A monadic operator takes one operand, on its left, as in `+/`. Monad and Dyad name the derived function's valences. Where both valences do the same thing, one name in the Monad column covers them. In the notes, `f` and `g` are functions, and `a`, `n` and `r` are arrays or numbers.

| Glyph | Key | Monad | Dyad | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` [slash](glyphs/slash.qmd) | | reduce | | `f/`, along the last axis. A left argument is a seed, as BQN’s `´` |
| `⌿` [slash-bar](glyphs/slash-bar.qmd) | Alt-Minus / | reduce-first | | `f⌿`, along the first axis. Seed as `/` |
| `\` [backslash](glyphs/backslash.qmd) | | scan | | `f\`, along the last axis. A left argument is a seed. Accumulates LTR as BQN |
| `⍀` [backslash-bar](glyphs/backslash-bar.qmd) | Alt-Minus Backslash | scan-first | | `f⍀`, along the first axis. Seed as `\`. Accumulates LTR as BQN |
| `¨` [diaeresis](glyphs/diaeresis.qmd) | Alt-1 | each | | `f¨` |
| `ᵇ` [superscript-b](glyphs/superscript-b.qmd) | Alt-6 b | bitwise | | `fᵇ` applies a Boolean function to integer bits |
| `⍨` [tilde-diaeresis](glyphs/tilde-diaeresis.qmd) | Alt-1 Backtick | self | commute | `f⍨`. `a⍨` is a constant function |
| `⊗` [circle-times](glyphs/circle-times.qmd) | Alt-o m | outer-product | | `g⊗`, as BQN's `⌜` |
| `⌸` [quad-equal](glyphs/quad-equal.qmd) | Alt-q = | key | | `f⌸` |
| `⇄` [right-left-arrows](glyphs/right-left-arrows.qmd) | Alt-4 | optimize | | `f⇄` searches for the point where `f` is least, or with `"solve":$t`, where its residuals are zero. A left argument holds options |
| `∂` [partial](glyphs/partial.qmd) | Alt-f | derivative | | `f∂` gives the Jacobian. The dyad differentiates `⍺ f ⍵` with respect to `⍵` |

## Dyadic operators

A dyadic operator takes an operand on each side, as in `f⍤1`. The columns are as for monadic operators.

| Glyph | Key | Monad | Dyad | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `↣` [right-tail-arrow](glyphs/right-tail-arrow.qmd) | Alt-. | before | | `f↣g`. `a↣f` binds a left argument. As BQN's `⊸` |
| `↢` [left-tail-arrow](glyphs/left-tail-arrow.qmd) | Alt-, | after | | `f↢g`. `f↢a` binds a right argument. As BQN's `⟜` |
| `⍤` [jot-diaeresis](glyphs/jot-diaeresis.qmd) | Alt-1 t | rank | | `f⍤r`, `f⍤g`. Rank 0 preserves atom/scalar distinction |
| `∘` [jot](glyphs/jot.qmd) | Alt-t | atop | | `f∘g`, as BQN's `∘` |
| `⍠` [quad-colon](glyphs/quad-colon.qmd) | Alt-q ; | axis | | `f⍠A`, `f⍠g` apply `f` along named or numbered axes |
| `⍥` [circle-diaeresis](glyphs/circle-diaeresis.qmd) | Alt-1 o | over | | `f⍥g` |
| `.` [dot](glyphs/dot.qmd) | | determinant | inner-product | `f.g`. The monad is J's determinant form, `u .v`. Also array fields and indexing |
| `⍣` [star-diaeresis](glyphs/star-diaeresis.qmd) | Alt-1 8 | power | | `f⍣n` iterates or inverts, `f⍣∞` finds a fixed point, `f⍣g` repeats until `g`, and `f⍣[g]` keeps the history until `g`. List counts give history, as J/BQN |
| `⊘` [circle-slash](glyphs/circle-slash.qmd) | Alt-o / | valences | | `f⊘g` calls `f` with one argument and `g` with two, as BQN's `⊘` |
| `⍚` [diamond-underbar](glyphs/diamond-underbar.qmd) | Alt-Minus Backtick | agenda | | `selector⍚cases` calls the function that the selector picks, as BQN's `◶`, or one for each cell |
| `@` [at](glyphs/at.qmd) | | under | | `f@g`, `f@a`, `f@[p]` apply `f` under a selection, positions, mask or transform. As BQN's `⌾`, not Dyalog's `@` |
| `⌺` [quad-diamond](glyphs/quad-diamond.qmd) | Alt-q Backtick | stencil | | `f⌺a`, `f⌺g` |

## Syntax and literals

| Glyph | Key | Name | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `←` [left-arrow](glyphs/left-arrow.qmd) | Alt-h | assign | Includes modified and selective assignment |
| `(…)` [parentheses](glyphs/parentheses.qmd) | | | Grouping. With `⋄`, a vector of rows: `(4⋄4 5)` is `[[4] [4 5]]` |
| `[…]` [brackets](glyphs/brackets.qmd) | | | Vectors and arrays: `[a b c]`, `[a;b c]`, `[1 2⋄3 4]`. One item makes a one-item vector: `[x]` is `,⊂x` |
| `{…}` [braces](glyphs/braces.qmd) | | | Defined function or operator. `;` separates its bodies |
| `⍺` [alpha](glyphs/alpha.qmd), `⍵` [omega](glyphs/omega.qmd) | Alt-a, Alt-w | left-argument, right-argument | |
| `⍶` [alpha-underbar](glyphs/alpha-underbar.qmd), `⍹` [omega-underbar](glyphs/omega-underbar.qmd) | Alt-Minus a, Alt-Minus w | left-operand, right-operand | |
| `∇` [del](glyphs/del.qmd), `⍢` [del-diaeresis](glyphs/del-diaeresis.qmd) | Alt-g, Alt-1 g | recursion, operator-recursion | A dfn's own function or operator |
| `?` [question](glyphs/question.qmd) | | predicate | Inside dfns |
| `::` [error-guard](glyphs/error-guard.qmd) | | | Error guard inside dfns |
| `⋄` [diamond](glyphs/diamond.qmd) | Alt-Backtick | separator | Separates statements, rows inside brackets, and rows of a vector inside parentheses |
| `⁝` [tricolon](glyphs/tricolon.qmd) | Alt-: | token-separator | Separates tokens without ending the run or continuing a literal strand |
| `⍝` [lamp](glyphs/lamp.qmd) | Alt-o c | comment | |
| `⎕←` [quad](glyphs/quad.qmd) | Alt-q | io | Explicit output. Read alone, the next line of input |
| `•` [bullet](glyphs/bullet.qmd) | Alt-y | system | [System function](system-functions.qmd) prefix |
| `⍬` [zilde](glyphs/zilde.qmd) | Alt-Shift-0 | empty | Empty numeric vector |
| `'…'` `"…"` [quote](glyphs/quote.qmd) | | | Character and string literals |
| `¯` [overbar](glyphs/overbar.qmd) | Alt-Minus | negative | Negative literal sign |
| `∞` [infinity](glyphs/infinity.qmd) | Alt-8 | | Real infinity |
| `$t` `$f` `$n` [constants](system/constants.qmd) | | | True, false and NaN |
| `$e` [caught error](system/constants.qmd) | | | The error a guard's handler caught |
| `²` `⁻¹` `ᵀ` `ᵘ` [superscript](scripts.ipynb#superscripts) | Alt-6 | | Postfix on the token before it, or after a space on the run before it: `x²` is `x*2`, `f²` is `f⍣2`, `f⁻¹` is the inverse of `f`, `mᵀ` is `⍉m`, and `fᵘ` is a scalar holding `f` |
| `₁` `₋₁` [subscript](scripts.ipynb#subscripts) | Alt-5 | | Postfix on the array before it, or after a space on the run before it: `v₁` is `1⌷v`, `v₋₁` is the last major cell, and `v₁←5` assigns to that cell |

[Numbers](numbers.qmd) covers numeric notation, such as `ₓ`, `r`, `j` and `e`.

## System names

System names start with `•`. [System functions](system-functions.qmd) lists them.

## Language-wide differences from Dyalog APL

- [Vectors](glyphs/brackets.qmd): a bracket list such as `[a b c]` is a vector. A strand of literals, such as `1 2 3`, needs no brackets. `[5]` is a one-item vector, the same as `,5`. [Parentheses](glyphs/parentheses.qmd) group: `(5)` is `5`. A scalar holding `5` is `⊂5`. Arrays side by side also form a vector: `a b` is `[a b]`. `(1 2⋄3)` is the vector of rows `[[1 2] [3]]`.
- [Runs](syntax.qmd#runs): outside brackets, spaces group an expression into runs, and each run acts as one token. A run that ends in a function is a train: `+/÷≢` is the mean, and `2×` is `2↣×`. An operator takes the token next to it, so after a run that ends in a dyadic operator, the next run is its right operand: in `⌊@ 10× x`, it is `10×`.
- [Indexing](glyphs/squad.qmd): brackets are used to write vectors, never to index. Positions and axes count from 0. Negative positions and axes count from the end. Index selects: `0⌷v` is the first item of `v`.
- [Atoms](arrays.ipynb): numbers, characters and functions are atoms, distinct from scalars, as BQN. Enclosing always adds a layer: `⊂3 ≡ 3` is `$f`.
- [Numbers](numbers.qmd): bare numbers are approximate. `ₓ` marks an exact integer, and `r` or `ᵣ` an exact rational, as in J: `1ₓ÷3ₓ` is `1ᵣ3`. Predicates, positions, tally and shape are exact. See [Mathish mode](numbers.qmd#mathish-mode) for comparison and zero-division conventions.
- [Agreement](evaluation.qmd#agreement-and-pervasion): pervasive functions, Each and Rank align leading axes. An axis of length 1 expands to match: `2 3⍴⍳6 + 10 20` is `[10 11 12⋄23 24 25]`.
- [Major cells](principles.ipynb#functions-act-on-major-cells): `∊ ~ ∪ ∩` compare major cells, `N#Y` replicates them, `N⊂Y` and `N⊆Y` split along the first axis. `⊤` and `⊥` put digits on the last axis, as J.
- [System names](system-functions.qmd): written `•name`, as BQN, not `⎕NAME`. Most Dyalog system functions and variables are not included.
- [Axis keys](keyed.ipynb) name data. `K:Y` evaluates its keys. `T.a` is `"a"⊃T`. `T.(expr)` and `T⍎Y` evaluate with the keys of `T` as names.
- [Dfns](dfns.ipynb): BPL has dfns, with no tradfns and no colon control structures such as `:If`.
- Removed forms: Dyalog's bracket axes `f[A]`, outer product `∘.f`, windowed reduce and laminate are not in BPL. Use [`⍠`](glyphs/quad-colon.qmd) for axes, [`⊗`](glyphs/circle-times.qmd) for outer products, [`↕`](glyphs/up-down-arrow.qmd) for windows, as in `+/3↕v`, and `[x⋄y]` for rows. `/ ⌿ \ ⍀` are only reduce and scan. A left argument to them is a seed, as in BQN: `2+/1 2 3` is `8`. Replicate and expand are [`#`](glyphs/hash.qmd) and `#⁻¹`.
